stories.title: Tata Steel to acquire 26.6% stake in APL Apollo for ₹15,510 crore
stories.summary: Tata Steel will acquire a 26.6 percent stake in APL Apollo Tubes for ₹15,510 crore. The deal includes an open offer for an additional 26 percent stake and the consolidation of Tata Steel's downstream businesses under APL Apollo. The company expects the move to drive future growth.

stories.title: Ashok Leyland plans truck plant in Singur
stories.summary: Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar announced that Ashok Leyland will establish a heavy vehicle manufacturing plant in Singur. The project follows preliminary discussions between the company and the West Bengal government. Officials have cautioned against premature announcements, noting that the state intends to prioritize projects that are actually implemented.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu introduces TN-TREND reform agenda
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu has launched TN-TREND, a reform agenda designed to simplify regulatory procedures and accelerate business approvals. The initiative focuses on six pillars, including digitisation and the elimination of redundant no-objection certificates. The state aims to strengthen its business ecosystem ahead of the upcoming Vettri Investment Conversion and Conclave.

stories.title: Machan founders enter luxury housing market in Mulshi
stories.summary: The founders of Machan Resorts are launching Aqua Vie, a private estate community near Lake Mulshi with an estimated retail value of over ₹600 crore. The project features 26 residential estates. The region has seen increased interest following land purchases by several high-profile celebrity investors.

stories.title: India-EU trade deal expected in December
stories.summary: India and the European Union are expected to sign a Free Trade Agreement during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Europe in December. The signing would follow the conclusion of negotiations in January. The Prime Minister is scheduled to undertake a four-nation tour for strategic bilateral and multilateral engagements.

stories.title: Tata Steel restructures downstream business with APL Apollo deal
stories.summary: Tata Steel plans to acquire a 26.38 percent stake in APL Apollo Tubes for ₹15,510.6 crore. The company will also launch an open offer for another 26 percent stake, potentially granting it majority control. The restructuring aims to consolidate Tata Steel's downstream operations under the structural steel tube manufacturer.

stories.title: Karnataka pledges support for Toyota expansion
stories.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar has assured Toyota Motor Corporation of state support for expanding its manufacturing operations. The company is reportedly considering scaling its local production capacity to one million vehicles. Officials discussed new mobility solutions and manufacturing footprint expansion during a meeting in Japan.

Brookfield to acquire India's PGP Glass from Blackstone for $1.7 billion - Reuters
Tata Steel details three-tranche acquisition of APL Apollo stake
stories.summary: Tata Steel will acquire a 26.6 percent stake in APL Apollo Tubes for ₹15,510 crore. The purchase of 73.8 million shares from the promoter group will occur in three tranches, concluding by 31 March 2028. The steelmaker intends to increase its presence in higher-value downstream products.

stories.title: Investors sell off Tata Steel and APL Apollo shares
stories.summary: Tata Steel will acquire a 26.4 percent stake in APL Apollo for ₹155.1 billion. The company claims the deal will boost downstream integration to 53 percent and improve product margins. Investors responded by sending Tata Steel shares down 9 percent and APL Apollo shares down 19 percent.

stories.title: Tata Steel announces strategic partnership with APL Apollo
stories.summary: Tata Steel will acquire a 26.6 percent promoter stake in APL Apollo for ₹15,510 crore. The deal includes an open offer for an additional 26 percent stake and a partnership to build 5 million tonnes of colour-coated steel capacity. The company is also offloading its existing tube and coating businesses.

stories.title: Tata Steel and APL Apollo shares fall on acquisition news
stories.summary: Tata Steel shares dropped 4.3 percent following the announcement of a ₹15,510 crore deal to acquire a 26.6 percent stake in APL Apollo Tubes. The acquisition could lead to a total investment of ₹32,266 crore if the subsequent open offer is fully subscribed. Markets reacted with a sell-off.

stories.title: Sejal Glass acquires Magnumtuff business for ₹40.80 crore
stories.summary: Sejal Glass has entered a business transfer agreement to acquire the architectural and automotive glass business of Magnumtuff India. The deal includes factory land and buildings in the Belagavi district of Karnataka. The acquisition is structured as a slump sale on a going-concern basis.

stories.title: Welspun Living approves ₹3,200 crore capital expenditure
stories.summary: Welspun Living shares reached a 52-week high of ₹278.75 after the board approved a ₹3,200 crore investment for its subsidiary, Welspun Home Solutions. Meanwhile, the India VIX volatility gauge surged 7.6 percent as benchmark indices traded lower amid a broader sell-off in metal and banking stocks.

stories.title: Indian markets slip as global sell-off impacts indices
stories.summary: Indian benchmark indices reversed early gains on Monday, with the Sensex dropping over 1,000 points. Over 2,600 stocks declined on the BSE during the mid-session. The market decline was broad-based, with significant selling pressure observed across banking and metal sectors as global sentiment weighed on local investors.

stories.title: Dalal Street sees profit booking after four-week rally
stories.summary: Indian benchmark indices declined on Monday as investors booked profits following a four-week rally. The Sensex fell 1,000 points from the previous close, while the Nifty Bank index dropped 2.18 percent. Despite the broader market decline, Tata Consultancy Services and Tech Mahindra shares rose nearly 3 percent.

stories.title: Sensex and Nifty decline as banking and metal stocks fall
stories.summary: The BSE Sensex fell 1,041 points and the Nifty 50 dropped below 25,500 on Monday. Selling pressure in the banking, financial services and metal sectors drove the indices lower. Tata Steel, Axis Bank and Hindalco Industries were among the top losers during the afternoon trading session.

stories.title: Sensex drops as profit booking hits bank shares
stories.summary: Benchmark indices fell on November 23 as profit booking emerged following a gap-up opening. The Sensex shed 1,077 points, while the Nifty declined 1.27 percent. Bank Nifty fell over 1,300 points after reaching a new high earlier in the day. Markets occasionally move in both directions.

stories.title: Sensex closes lower as metal sector drags
stories.summary: The BSE Sensex dropped 1,059 points to close at 82,860, marking a 1.26 percent decline. The index remains 3.98 percent below its 52-week high. While the index holds above its 50-day moving average, the 50-day average is now positioned below the 200-day average, signaling a cautious trend.

stories.title: Market slide wipes out Rs 5.33 lakh crore
stories.summary: Indian equity benchmarks snapped a winning streak on Monday, with the Sensex falling over 1,100 points. The decline wiped out Rs 5.33 lakh crore in investor wealth, bringing the total market capitalization of BSE-listed companies to Rs 509 lakh crore. Profit booking and global cues were cited as factors.

stories.title: Asian markets decline as chipmakers shed value
stories.summary: Asian markets fell as investors tracked a sell-off in technology stocks. South Korean chipmakers led the decline, shedding approximately 3 percent in early trading. The movement follows a broader trend of cooling sentiment toward the sector.

stories.title: Seoul shares plunge over 3 pct on AI jitters - upi
Global markets face turmoil as AI boom cracks
stories.summary: Global markets are reeling following Wall Street's worst week since 2020. Investors are questioning whether massive investments in AI data centers will generate sufficient returns. While U.S. stock futures offered a positive signal, Asian markets fell by as much as 5 percent early Monday.

stories.title: Asian regulators monitor sagging markets
stories.summary: Asian regulators are moving to support regional markets as sentiment toward the AI trade falters. Hardware suppliers and chipmakers are described as particularly vulnerable to the shift in investor confidence. The intervention follows a period of significant volatility across global indices.

stories.title: Asian stocks slide as AI sell-off deepens
stories.summary: Asian stocks fell on Monday as the AI sell-off extended from Wall Street. South Korea's Kospi slid 3.2 percent, while Hong Kong and Shanghai indices also saw declines. The S&P 500 entered a correction on Friday, defined as a fall of at least 10 percent from recent highs.

stories.title: Tech stocks struggle as Wall Street rout continues
stories.summary: The Nasdaq has lost nearly a fifth of its value since hitting a record high last month. Despite strong earnings from Nvidia and a blockbuster IPO from Anthropic, selling pressure persists. Traders are now tracking further potential interest rate hikes and tighter regulation in the United States.

stories.title: RBI governor meets NBFC leaders to discuss funding
stories.summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra is meeting with executives from non-banking financial companies, housing finance companies, and microfinance institutions today. The agenda includes sector challenges and requests for a refinancing fund using bank priority sector lending shortfalls, alongside tax exemptions on interest payments.

stories.title: CERT-In warns of AI-assisted cyberattacks
stories.summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team has warned that threat actors are using AI to target ICT assets. The attacks have resulted in unauthorized financial transactions at banking and technology firms by compromising business records and approval processes. The systems involved were otherwise legitimate.

stories.title: RBI reviews cybersecurity at NBFCs
stories.summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra and his deputies are meeting with NBFC executives to examine cybersecurity preparedness. The central bank is concerned about vulnerabilities in digital lending systems and security risks linked to third-party payment interfaces. The meeting follows reports of increasing threats to financial institutions.

stories.title: RBI governor holds annual meeting with NBFCs
stories.summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra is meeting with senior executives from non-banking financial companies today. Industry sources describe the event as an annual interaction where representatives share sector developments and emerging challenges. The regulator is expected to listen to concerns regarding the current financial landscape.

stories.title: RBI monitors gold loan portfolios
stories.summary: The RBI has increased monitoring of gold loan portfolios at banks and NBFCs following a correction in bullion prices. Some loan-to-value ratios have reportedly breached 100 percent as gold values fell. The central bank is tracking the potential impact on defaults.

stories.title: Three private banks face margin pressure
stories.summary: Rising repo rates and inflation are placing pressure on Indian private sector banks. Analysts suggest the current macro environment is reshaping funding costs and loan demand. The sector is being monitored for potential risks as growth expectations adjust to a tougher reality.

stories.title: RBI rate hikes reshape bank valuations
stories.summary: Higher interest rates and cooler GDP growth are impacting the risk and reward mix for large-cap private sector banks. While some lenders may benefit from higher yields, others face pressure on loan growth. Investors are currently evaluating which institutions are most exposed to these shifts.

stories.title: EPFO to enable UPI-based withdrawals
stories.summary: The EPFO is finalizing a feature to allow provident fund withdrawals via the BHIM app by the end of December. The update is part of the EPFO 3.0 technology upgrade. Trials have reportedly been completed, and developers have addressed glitches encountered during the testing phase.

stories.title: EPFO approves systematic withdrawal plan for retirees
stories.summary: The Employees Provident Fund Organisation has approved a systematic withdrawal plan for retiring members, allowing for regular payouts instead of a lump sum. The board also greenlit easier premature withdrawal rules and direct voluntary contributions. The retirement fund is now offering a choice in how to receive savings.

stories.title: Wise raises Malaysia wallet limit to RM50,000
stories.summary: Wise has increased its wallet limit for Malaysian customers to RM50,000, which the company claims is the highest in the country. The firm is also running a year-end campaign offering cash prizes for overseas spending. Holding more travel money is now officially encouraged.

stories.title: Ambit Capital prefers Pine Labs over Paytm
stories.summary: Brokerage firm Ambit Capital has shifted its preference toward Pine Labs over Paytm, citing revenue diversification and valuation comfort. While Pine Labs shares gained, Paytm parent One97 Communications declined. Industry discussions now suggest a flat fee structure for business-to-business digital payments is on the horizon.

stories.title: AI tools complicate UPI fraud prevention
stories.summary: UPI has become the standard for Indian payments, but authorities report that generative AI is making fraud harder to control. Scammers are using the technology to clone voices and impersonate trusted individuals at scale. The convenience of instant transfers now comes with an automated threat.

stories.title: Monzo alums' fraud startup Acorda raises £1.8M pre-seed - Dealroom
India showcases fintech at Singapore festival
stories.summary: The India Pavilion at the Singapore FinTech Festival highlighted the nation's digital public infrastructure and financial technology startups. Under the theme Bharat SETU, the event focused on cross-border business opportunities and international partnerships. India is positioning its digital stack as a bridge to the future.

stories.title: Parag Parikh launches GIFT City feeder fund for NRIs
stories.summary: PPFAS has opened a US dollar-denominated feeder fund in GIFT City, allowing overseas investors to access its flagship flexi cap fund without an Indian bank account. The minimum investment is $10,000. It is a way to invest in Indian stocks without actually touching India.

stories.title: EPFO to allow systematic withdrawals for retirees
stories.summary: EPFO subscribers will soon be able to opt for a systematic withdrawal plan to receive retirement savings in monthly, quarterly or half-yearly instalments. The move aims to replace the traditional lump sum withdrawal. Retirees can now choose how slowly they want to spend their money.

stories.title: Kiyosaki advises waiting for asset price crash
stories.summary: Author Robert Kiyosaki has advised investors to wait for the current slide in gold, silver and bitcoin prices to end before buying. He compared purchasing volatile assets during a downturn to grabbing a falling knife. The Fed and major investment banks are blamed for the market conditions.

stories.title: Gold and silver prices rebound in domestic trade
stories.summary: Gold and silver prices rose in early domestic trading following a recovery from 14-month lows. Bullion gained 2.6 percent internationally as a tech-stock rout drove investors toward haven assets. The precious metals market is currently reacting to the broader movement of US Treasury yields.

stories.title: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO reaches 88 percent subscription
stories.summary: The Mahanadi Coalfields initial public offering reached 88 percent subscription on its final day of bidding. The 8,981 crore sale consists entirely of an offer-for-sale by promoter Coal India. Since the IPO involves no new shares, the company will receive none of the proceeds.

stories.title: Crystal Crop Protection IPO allotment expected today
stories.summary: The allotment for the 455 crore Crystal Crop Protection IPO is expected to be finalised today following a 17-time subscription. Non-institutional investors led the demand for the issue. Shares were recently commanding a grey market premium of 14.5 rupees.

stories.title: Crystal Crop Protection IPO allotment finalised
stories.summary: Crystal Crop Protection has finalised the allotment for its 455 crore public issue after receiving bids for 17 times the shares on offer. Non-institutional investors accounted for the highest demand. The company is scheduled to list its shares on the stock exchanges on November 26.

stories.title: New GDP series aims to improve policy accuracy
stories.summary: The government has introduced a revised GDP series with a 2022-23 base year, incorporating wider data sources and double deflation. The update aims to reduce volatility in economic estimates and help the Reserve Bank of India calibrate monetary policy. More stable data is the stated goal.

stories.title: RBI expects new GDP series to stabilise estimates
stories.summary: Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta stated that the revised GDP series will produce more stable estimates with smaller revisions. The methodology is intended to support better-calibrated monetary policy decisions by the Reserve Bank of India. Early estimates are now expected to be less prone to future correction.

stories.title: Revised GDP and CPI series to guide policy
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India expects the new GDP and CPI series to provide a more accurate picture of the evolving economic structure. Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said the updated base year and expanded data will help reduce inflation volatility. Policy decisions are set to become more data-driven.

stories.title: New GDP series narrows demand and supply gap
stories.summary: Reserve Bank of India Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said the revised GDP series has successfully narrowed the discrepancy between demand and supply estimates. The previous series was noted for large and volatile gaps. The economy is now being measured with a tighter focus on alignment.

stories.title: Hiring trends point to 2027 job growth
stories.summary: The consumer electronics, retail and manufacturing sectors are forecast to grow by 12 to 14 percent in 2027. Overall hiring activity is projected to rise by 8.2 percent, with demand focused on operations and supply chain roles. A broader recovery is expected across the job market.

stories.title: India white-collar hiring projected to reach 1.38 crore in 2027
stories.summary: India's white-collar job market is expected to grow 8.16 percent in 2027, reaching 1.38 crore total jobs, according to the foundit Insights Tracker. This follows a 3.30 percent increase in 2026. The forecast assumes the current pace of acceleration will hold for the next year.

stories.title: India manufacturing growth offsets services slowdown in November
stories.summary: The HSBC Flash India Composite PMI rose to 56.3 in November, driven by a nine-month high in manufacturing activity. While factory output and hiring increased, the services sector saw a slight decline in growth. The economy is currently expanding, though at a more modest pace than earlier this year.

research.title: Accountable AI Delegation in Banking: Identity, Commitment Controls, Decision Evidence and Recovery
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: An AI-assisted payment can pass assessment and lose release authority before commitment. We specify a banking delegation contract that checks current authority, the shared payment cap and the capacity of eligible instruments to cover losses. It. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are expected to complete tasks while following rules of conduct, but these objectives can conflict. We study how evolutionary selection shapes an agent's choices between them, and whether experience can make those. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Keeping in Place After the Storm-Emergency Assistance and Evictions
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: We offer evidence that federal emergency assistance (FEMA) in the days following natural disasters mitigate evictions in comparison to similar emergency scenarios where FEMA aid is not provided. We find an approximate 10.9% increase in overall. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Rethinking Arrow--Debreu: A New Framework for Exchange
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper revisits the Arrow--Debreu general equilibrium framework through the lens of effective trade, emphasizing the distinction between theoretical and realizable market interactions. We develop the Effective Trade Model (ETM), where transactions arise from bilateral feasibility. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Science under Threat? A Natural Experiment in Economics
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Academic freedom is under strain worldwide. To study how scholars respond to (perceived) political pressure, we exploit a natural experiment in the United States: the publication in early 2025 of a "stop list" of words flagged. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: The Rise of Agents and the Human Labor Market
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide the first economy-wide and cross-AI model evidence on the effects of agentic AI on labor demand. We combine proprietary OpenRouter data covering about two quadrillion tokens of realized AI consumption (2 percent of global. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: The Rural Margin of Territorial Peace: Within-Municipality Evidence from Colombia
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Colombia's peace agreement introduced participatory development programs and congressional constituencies reserved for conflict victims with a rural electorate. I use repeated waves of the Social Capital Barometer and a triple-difference event study to compare changes in. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Trust and Lottery-Related Anomalies
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: We examine whether social trust shapes the pricing of lottery-like stocks by influencing investors' beliefs regarding optimistic information associated with extreme future payoffs. We argue that higher social trust reduces investors' skepticism toward optimistic information associated. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
